theCapabilityClaim.v1Defect: B-FI-05, critical. v1 listed what the imperative Rule API does not hand you — filesystem, network, spawn, clock, entropy, storage, cross-rule results — and called that an absence of ambient authority. That is Error 2 for the third time in this exercise: a narrow handle does not confine LINKED code, which reaches the same capabilities through its own imports, transitive dependencies, module globals, native calls, or an injected collaborator.
theCapabilityClaim.accurateClaim: For linked first-party rules: **these capabilities are NOT PROVIDED BY the Rule API, and the rule's direct dependency closure is audited.** That is an integrity control, not a security boundary, and it is the strongest true statement available without a restricted runtime.
theCapabilityClaim.whatWouldMakeItABoundary: Executing every imperative rule in a named capability-restricted process or component runtime, with direct, transitive AND dynamic reach tested there. That runtime does not exist; ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT is REOPENED over exactly this.
theCapabilityClaim.conformanceConsequence: FI-07 is marked implementable:false and its blocker named. v1 asserted it as a passing closure analysis, which would have been a paper seal.
theCapabilityClaim.whatIsStillTrue: The API not providing a capability still means an ordinary rule cannot casually acquire one, and dependency-closure audit still catches the common case. The claim is narrower, not empty.

thirdPartyImperativeRules.rule: Untrusted/third-party imperative rules are disabled for authoritative Runs until a named capability-restricted runtime is selected and tested over direct, transitive, dynamic, native, and collaborator reach. Linked first-party rules remain TCB code under dependency audit.
thirdPartyImperativeRules.architectureSummaryMustSay: API supplies facts only; linked first-party rules are accepted TCB; dependency audit is integrity control; third-party imperative rules are excluded until ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT resolves.

normalisationLadder.form: A ladder of named, independently versioned levels, not one policy.
normalisationLadder.why: Exact-duplicate and near-duplicate detection want different normalisation; forcing one loses precision or recall permanently.

levels.normalises: nothing — raw bytes of the body span
L2 plus consistent renaming of LOCAL bindings

rules.rule: Each level is separately versioned. Changing L2's comment grammar does not touch L1 identities.
The level and its version are part of the fact's identity and enter the derivation key. Two levels are two facts, never one fact computed differently.
A finding records the level that produced it. Comparing a baseline entry pinned to L1 against an L2 result is a typed mismatch, not a diff.
Adding a level is schema-additive and changes no existing identity.
Changing an EXISTING level's algorithm requires the custody transition protocol below. There is no migrator that can invent the old identity from the new one.
The L0 span LOCATION is retrievable for any finding at any level. Retrieving its BYTES is a separate, retention-governed act (B-FI-04).

custodyTransition.v1Defect: B-FI-01 and B-FI-02, both critical. v1 said the ladder was reversible because levels are additive. Additivity avoids silent false net-new findings; it does NOT preserve the user's ratchet, because the hard transition is merely deferred to baseline re-capture. And BH-5 demanded a migrator that may have no information from which to compute the new identity at all.
custodyTransition.narrowerTruth: Level addition is SCHEMA-ADDITIVE, not CUSTODY-REVERSIBLE.

algorithmChangeToExistingLevel.step1: Continue evaluating the OLD level version for a declared support window. Both versions are live; identities do not collide because the version is in the identity (BH-2).
algorithmChangeToExistingLevel.step2: Emit the new version's grouping as a PREVIEW, never as policy.
algorithmChangeToExistingLevel.step3: Require explicit user acceptance before the new version acquires policy identity.
algorithmChangeToExistingLevel.step4: On acceptance, record the transition with a many-to-many group mapping between old and new duplicate groups.
algorithmChangeToExistingLevel.ifNoWitness: Where no retained witness supports a mapping, the comparison is reported INDETERMINATE and re-baselining is required. This is stated rather than papered: a migrator that cannot see the old inputs cannot produce the old identity, and pretending otherwise is how a silent re-identification ships.

minimum: occurrenceAnchors: L0 span-location set per group
deterministicEdgeOrder: sort by oldGroupId, newGroupId, class

projection.userFacing: deterministic split/merge summaries with drill-down to occurrence anchors
projection.forbids: one-to-one falsification of a many-to-many relation

migrationWitness.honesty: This witness supports a many-to-many mapping. It does NOT support recomputing an old identity from new inputs.

protocol.groupTransitionModel: MANY-TO-MANY. A normalisation change can split one group, merge two, or both. User readability is supplied by deterministic split/merge summaries plus drill-down, not by falsifying the relation as one-to-one.

languageCapability.v1Defect: B-FI-03. v1 named L1/L2/L3 as if they were language-independent. 'Insignificant whitespace' is not a language-independent notion, and neither is 'comment'.
languageCapability.rule: Each level is implementable per language at a declared capability. A language that cannot implement a level MUST report Coverage with the fact-plane deficiency vocabulary — never a silent approximation.

matrix.note: R2-FI-05: L2/L3 full only after directive/JSDoc corpora; provisional until then.
Indentation is SIGNIFICANT, so L1 may not normalise leading whitespace. L3 needs binding resolution beyond the syntax tier.
Build-constraint comments are directives, not comments. R2-FI-05: semicolon insertion requires token-aware L1; provisional until measured.

languageCapability.significantLayoutRule: A level MUST NOT normalise layout that is semantically significant in the target language. Python indentation is the canonical case; anything inside a string literal is universal.
languageCapability.directiveRule: Comment-shaped DIRECTIVES are classified separately from removable comments and are NEVER removed at L2. Examples: Go build constraints, TypeScript triple-slash references and ts-ignore, Rust inner attributes and doc comments feeding cfg, Python encoding declarations and type comments. Removing a directive changes meaning, so removing it at a level advertised as comment-insensitive would make two semantically different bodies identical.
neverNormalise: layout that is significant in the language

capabilityGrades.full: the contract requires full language semantics; an implementation may advertise this grade only after adversarial golden-corpus agreement across two producers
capabilityGrades.full-provisional: judgment from language spec; MUST be treated as restricted for shipping identity claims until measured
capabilityGrades.restricted: known semantic caveats; identity equivalence only within declared constraints
capabilityGrades.unavailable: must emit language-tier-unsupported deficiency; never silent approximation

languageCapability.productScopeRule: supportedLanguages is the architecture capability matrix, not the v1 installed-language set. v1 admits TypeScript and Rust only. Python or Go identity production requires an explicit later product scope change plus the corresponding corpus evidence before admission.
languageCapability.bindingRule: Exactly one matrix row per supportedLanguages entry. Every (language, level) cell MUST have a levelFixture whose expected capability equals the matrix cell (full-provisional may fixture as restricted for shipping behavior). Deleting a row or desynchronizing a fixture fails FI-CAP (R2-FI-02).

anchorValidation.v1Defect: B-FI-06. v1 said an imperative rule 'cannot compute or influence a fingerprint'. It cannot MINT the final fingerprint — it does not choose the hash. But it chooses the ANCHORS, so a buggy or hostile rule can still destabilise or collide its own identities by emitting different or fabricated anchors.
anchorValidation.accurateClaim: A rule cannot mint a fingerprint. The HOST resolves and validates every typed anchor before computing one.
hostObligations: resolve each anchor reference against retained facts and snapshot provenance
reject anchors that do not resolve — a fabricated anchor is a rule defect, not a finding
reject anchors outside the rule's declared scope
enforce a per-rule-family anchor schema, so a rule cannot silently change anchor shape between versions
anchorValidation.residual: A rule can still emit fewer anchors than it should, producing unstable-but-valid identities. That is a rule quality problem, detectable by fingerprint churn, and not something the host can prevent.

budgetModel.v1Defect: B-FI-07. v1 let exhaustion produce a Coverage entry over whatever findings had already been emitted. Different scheduling then authorises different partial prefixes, and every outcome looks valid.
budgetModel.transactionality: Rule output is BUFFERED. On exhaustion the entire rule partition is discarded and reported, unless the rule contract explicitly supports complete pages with a continuation token. A partial prefix is never policy input.

dimensions.why: the real cost driver, and reproducible
the finding channel is exfiltration bandwidth and a denial-of-merge vector
NOT a semantic limit — it varies by machine. Recorded in Coverage when it fires, never used to define a valid partial result.

budgetModel.semanticLimitRule: Only deterministic budgets define outcomes. Wall clock is a backstop whose firing is recorded and which forces the same whole-partition discard.

onExhaustion.rule: Exhaustion NEVER silently truncates. Truncation without a marker converts a budget into a correctness bug.

budgetModel.attribution: Exhaustion names the rule and, where determinable, the input that drove it.

spanIdentityVersusBytes.v1Defect: B-FI-04. v1 made L0 byte retrievability an unconditional property of fact identity, which silently upgrades a structural-retention Run into a source archive — one duplicate rule and the retained set approaches read-set size.

separation.identity: L0 span LOCATION plus a content commitment. Always retained; contains no source bytes.
separation.bytes: Retrieved only when the Run's retention policy authorises it, and reported UNAVAILABLE after degradation rather than silently missing.

spanIdentityVersusBytes.rule: Byte retention is never an unconditional consequence of fact identity.

conformanceTests.assert: Two normalisation levels over one body produce two distinct fact identities, both retained.
A finding records its level; comparing an L1-pinned baseline against an L2 result is a typed mismatch, not a diff.
Adding a level changes no existing level's identities.
An algorithm change to an existing level without dual-emit and explicit user acceptance is refused by the release gate.
The L0 span LOCATION is retrievable for any finding at any level; byte retrieval is retention-governed and reports unavailable after degradation.
An imperative rule querying outside its declared requirements receives a typed error, not a wider result set.
An imperative rule has no reachable filesystem, network, spawn, clock, entropy, storage or cross-rule access, tested over direct, transitive AND dynamic paths.
conformanceTests.note: B-FI-05. v1 asserted this as a passing closure analysis. For LINKED code a dependency audit is an integrity control, not a security boundary, and claiming otherwise is Error 2.

conformanceTests.assert: Exhausting any deterministic budget discards the whole rule partition and produces a Coverage entry; findings are never silently truncated and no partial prefix becomes policy input.
A rule cannot MINT a fingerprint. An unresolvable or out-of-scope anchor is rejected as a rule defect before any fingerprint is computed.
A rule declared non-deterministic is excluded from digest-equality claims and its findings are marked.
A level a language cannot implement reports Coverage with a fact-plane deficiency; it never approximates silently.
No level normalises a comment-shaped directive, a string literal's contents, or layout significant in the language.
Two independent producers implementing the published canonicalisation agree byte-for-byte on every golden corpus entry.
Wall clock never defines a valid partial result; its firing is recorded in Coverage and forces the same whole-partition discard.

R2-FI-01: implementable tests specify the property; DISCHARGED requires demonstrated execution evidence which does not exist yet.

properties.property: a rule cannot influence its own identity

resolves.B-FI-01: RESOLVED — the narrower truth is stated: level addition is schema-additive, not custody-reversible. A four-step transition protocol with dual-emit, preview, and explicit user acceptance replaces the reversibility claim.
resolves.B-FI-02: RESOLVED — the migration witness is specified at its honest minimum, group transitions are modelled MANY-TO-MANY, and where no witness supports a mapping the comparison is INDETERMINATE and re-baselining is required. No migrator is asked to invent an old identity.
resolves.B-FI-03: RESOLVED — a per-language capability matrix, a significant-layout rule, and a directive classification separate from removable comments. An unimplementable level reports a fact-plane deficiency.
resolves.B-FI-04: RESOLVED — span LOCATION identity is separated from byte retrieval; byte retention is never an unconditional consequence of fact identity.
resolves.B-FI-05: RESOLVED BY RETRACTION — the absence claim is withdrawn. FI-07 is implementable:false with its blocker named, and the sealed property moves to NOT DISCHARGED. The accurate claim is 'not provided by the API, dependency closure audited'.
resolves.B-FI-06: RESOLVED — 'cannot compute or influence' becomes 'cannot MINT', with five host obligations for anchor resolution and validation, and the residual instability stated.
resolves.B-FI-07: RESOLVED — rule output is transactional and the whole partition is discarded on exhaustion; deterministic budgets define semantics and wall clock is a recorded backstop only.
resolves.B-FI-08: RESOLVED — TM.F3 replaced with live v2 references, checked mechanically by FI-TM; the body-identity hazard is stated as this artifact's own claim; C-2 dependency now points at the adjudicated v3.
resolves.B-FI-09: RESOLVED — a four-step byte-level canonicalisation with length-prefixed framing and domain separation, an explicit collision policy, and a per-language adversarial golden corpus requirement.

knownLimitations: The canonicalisation construction is specified; the per-language golden corpora it requires do not exist. FI-CANON checks the requirement is declared, not that the corpus is populated.
The language capability matrix covers four languages and is judgment, not measurement.
FI-07 is unimplementable and the corresponding property is NOT DISCHARGED. Third-party/untrusted imperative rules are excluded from v1 rather than shipped under a false confinement claim.
A rule emitting too few anchors still produces unstable identities; the host cannot prevent that.
The generic FACT-ID-V1 vectors are executable architecture oracles, not an independently implemented Rust host or provider qualification record.

factRecordIdentityBoundaryV1.purpose: Keep normalized source-body identity and generic admitted-fact identity as two composable contracts. A clone payload may carry a normalized body identity; the host then mints a distinct FACT-ID-V1 for the complete admitted fact record.

normalizedBodyIdentity.input: one normalized source body span plus level/language/version components

genericFactRecordIdentity.input: the exact fourteen-field admitted FactRecordV1 semantic preimage

clonePayloadJoin.rule: The normalized body identity is payload data inside a clones fact. FACT-ID-V1 wraps the complete clone fact and can never equal or substitute for bodyIdentity by type or domain.

separationRules: The two domain tags and contract identifiers are distinct and immutable within v1.
Normalized body identity never hashes FactEnvelope, relation payload, universes, confidence or anchors.
FACT-ID-V1 never re-runs body normalization; it hashes the already validated relation payload bytes and anchors, including bodyIdentity only when the relation schema carries it.
A provider may compute a candidate bodyIdentity under the pinned body grammar but never mints FACT-ID-V1; the host validates both boundaries.
factRecordIdentityBoundaryV1.assurance: IMPLEMENTABLE_UNEXECUTED; exact FACT-ID-V1 vectors live in FACT-PLANE and normalized-body corpora remain implementation evidence

canonicalisationSchema.v1Defect: B-FI-09. v1 named levels but published no byte-level construction, so two independent producers could implement different hashes and both claim conformance — destroying exactly the cross-version and cross-platform identity stability the ladder exists to provide.

construction.step1: Extract the body span at L0 byte boundaries.
construction.step2: For L0, the canonical payload is the raw body-span bytes with no tokenisation. For L1-L3, apply the level's declared transform to the versioned language token stream. Token boundaries, canonical kind IDs, and replacements are part of the level-version specification.
construction.step3: Serialise the selected payload with the byteGrammar below: raw length-prefixed bytes for L0, or a count-framed stream of length-prefixed canonical kind/value byte pairs for L1-L3.
construction.step4: Hash with DOMAIN SEPARATION over a FULLY FRAMED preimage: H(len-prefixed domainTag || len-prefixed levelId || len-prefixed levelVersion || len-prefixed languageId || len-prefixed languageVersion || len-prefixed payload). Unframed concatenation of the identity components is FORBIDDEN (R2-FI-03).

canonicalisationSchema.collisionPolicy: A hash collision between two distinct canonical payloads is a HOST DEFECT, reported as such and never resolved by preferring one. Framing makes distinct canonical payloads produce distinct preimages; an intended normalisation equivalence may map different source spans to the same canonical payload.
canonicalisationSchema.goldenCorpusRequirement: Each implementation must supply a versioned corpus for every language it admits, including adversarial significant whitespace, comment-shaped directives, string literals containing comment syntax, Unicode normalisation, and mixed line endings. TypeScript and Rust are required for v1; other matrix rows require evidence before a later product admission. FI-CANON checks that this obligation remains declared; retained corpus contents and execution records are implementation/qualification evidence, not architecture evidence fabricated by this checker.

byteGrammar.encoding: UTF-8 source bytes as read from the snapshot; no re-encoding
byteGrammar.unicodeNormalization: none at L0; NFC only if a level transform explicitly declares it
byteGrammar.lineEndings: L0 preserves CR/LF/CRLF as in the snapshot bytes; L1+ may normalise only where the language treats them as insignificant whitespace
byteGrammar.bodySpanBoundary: half-open byte offsets [start,end) into the snapshot file blob; end exclusive
byteGrammar.levelVersionDefinition: raw 32-byte SHA-256 content digest of the canonical level specification, including per-language lexical boundary rules, canonical token-kind registry, directive classification, transform order, and replacement byte rules; a human semantic-version label alone is insufficient

identifierEncoding.domainTag: exact ASCII bytes of the fixed domainTag literal
identifierEncoding.levelId: exact ASCII bytes of the enumerated normalisationLadder.level value
identifierEncoding.levelVersion: raw 32-byte digest defined by levelVersionDefinition, not hexadecimal display text
identifierEncoding.languageId: lowercase ASCII bytes of the languageCapability.matrix language id
identifierEncoding.languageVersion: exact canonical identity bytes supplied by ResolvedInputs/PlanId, not a human display string

payloadEncodingByLevel.L0-verbatim: u32be raw_byte_len || exact snapshot body-span bytes; tokenisation is forbidden

byteGrammar.tokenKindDefinition: kind_id is the non-empty UTF-8 canonical identifier from the token-kind registry committed by levelVersion; producer/toolchain numeric enum ordinals are forbidden
byteGrammar.tokenValueDefinition: value_bytes are the exact source lexeme bytes unless the level specification replaces them with declared canonical ASCII bytes; no implicit Unicode or encoding conversion is permitted
byteGrammar.tokenEncoding: each token = u16be kind_id_len || kind_id_bytes || u32be value_len || value_bytes
byteGrammar.languageVersionDefinition: the language toolchain/mode identity recorded in PlanId / ResolvedInputs for the provider interpreting the body span (e.g. typescript@X, rustc@Y edition Z); this identity remains framed for L0 even though its payload is raw bytes
byteGrammar.forbidden: raw string concatenation of levelId||levelVersion||languageId||languageVersion without length prefixes; tokenising L0; raw producer/toolchain numeric token-kind ordinals
